prompts.prompt: Create a two-panel symbolic WHITEBOARD concept diagram showing successive Newton quadratic approximations on the SAME objective landscape, based on the reference style. Pure white background, blue true objective f(x), thin gray dashed approximation curves, orange candidate dots, green minimizer x*, compact handwritten math labels only. The two panels are SIDE BY SIDE, landscape canvas about 3:2. They MUST use identical axes bounds and IDENTICAL blue nonquadratic bowl shape with a minimum at interior x*. Each panel has vertical f(x) axis at far left and horizontal x axis at bottom, no numeric ticks. LEFT panel: current orange actual point on far-right hillside labeled x_k beneath axis; gray dashed upward-opening quadratic q_k(x) touches actual blue curve at this current point with same value and tangent. Gray quadratic has vertex to LEFT of current but still RIGHT of actual minimum; hollow gray dot at model vertex. Dashed vertical down from vertex to actual blue curve gives next actual candidate x_(k+1), marked orange. Label gray curve q_k(x); show small orange STRAIGHT arrow from current actual candidate toward next actual candidate, indicating discrete update, not a path along curve. RIGHT panel: unchanged identical blue f(x); now current actual candidate is the same x_(k+1) as LEFT panel's result, with exactly same coordinates. NEW gray dashed quadratic q_(k+1)(x) matches at that candidate, with a new vertex further left, closer to x*. Project vertically to actual blue curve for next candidate x_(k+2); small orange straight update arrow connects the two actual candidates. Label gray curve q_(k+1)(x). Both panels label green true minimum's horizontal coordinate x*, and their two actual candidate horizontal coordinates. Use correct true subscripts k, k+1, k+2. Do NOT include any polynomial coefficients or numerical examples. No heading; captions belong in surrounding Markdown. No gray old approximation retained in right panel: show ONLY the newly fitted one. All type should be modest, uniform handwritten mathematical style, target about 14–16px when entire image is displayed at 440 CSS pixels wide. Keep generous separation between panels and do not crowd axis labels. This diagram must make clear that the objective stays FIXED but the approximation is recomputed after updating the decision variable.

Replace this numeric whiteboard stopping example with a compact SYMBOLIC stopping-check diagram. Square composition intended for 250–280 CSS pixels display width, lettering about 14–16px at that size. Top center: Korean label '현재 의사결정변수' and blue math x_k with real subscript. Down arrow to centered black formula |f′(x_k)| ≤ ε. Split into two arrows: left branch label '충족' to small teal rounded box '종료'; right branch label '미충족' to small orange rounded box '뉴턴 갱신', with x_(k+1) beneath label using proper subscript. A thin gray return arrow on far right connects update box back to top, without crossing content. The meaning is: check current gradient magnitude, stop if tolerance is met, otherwise update the decision variable and check again. Only the exact listed Korean labels and formulas. No checkmark implying a minimum guaranteed, no plots, no visualized code output, no large heading, no watermark. Keep whiteboard line style matching the reference but simplify its content.
